idea.body: Rounding a number means asking which friendly number it is closest to. Find the digit in the place you are rounding to, then look at the single digit right after it. That next digit is the only one that matters: 5 or more means round up, anything less means keep the rounding digit the same. Every digit after the rounding place becomes a zero, or gets dropped for decimals. This makes estimation fast: round each number in a calculation first, then work with the friendly numbers instead of the exact ones. A rover reading of 347 meters rounds to 350 to the nearest ten, since the digit after the tens place is 7.

workedExample.prompt: A print shop printed 3,482 pages this month. What is that rounded to the nearest hundred?
steps: The digit right after it, in the tens place, is 8.
8 is 5 or more, so round the hundreds digit up from 4 to 5.
Replace the tens and ones digits with zero.

ways.name: Round to the nearest place
ways.when: Use this when a problem asks you to round one number to a stated place.
steps: Find the digit in the place you are rounding to.
Look at the single digit right after it.
5 or more rounds that digit up by one; less than 5 leaves it the same.
Replace every digit after the rounding place with zero.
ways.trap: Rounding based on a digit two places away instead of the single digit right after the rounding place.

figure.alt: A number line from 3400 to 3500 with 3482 marked closer to the 3500 end, showing it rounds up to 3500.

frames.caption: Find the digit in the rounding place.
Look at the single digit right after it.
5 or more rounds up by one.
Replace digits after it with zero.

ways.name: Front-end estimation
ways.when: Use this for a fast estimate of a total, when exactness does not matter yet.
steps: Keep only the leading digit of each number and replace the rest with zeros.
Add or subtract those leading-digit numbers.
That rough total is your front-end estimate.
ways.trap: Treating the front-end estimate as exact instead of a fast, rough total.

ways.name: Round both, then adjust
ways.when: Use this when you rounded first but need a total closer to the exact answer.
steps: Round each number to the nearest hundred and note how much each rounding changed it.
Take back what a rounding added, and add back what a rounding removed.
That adjusted total is close to the exact answer.
ways.trap: Adjusting in the wrong direction, adding back what should be taken away.

ways.name: Compatible numbers
ways.when: Use this when the numbers are close to ones that combine cleanly.
steps: Change each number slightly to a nearby one that pairs nicely with the other.
Do the easy calculation with those compatible numbers.
Use that as your estimate, without adjusting further.
ways.trap: Picking compatible numbers so far from the originals that the estimate is not useful.
